text:
The Schur product of two codewords of the hyperderivative Reed–Solomon code corresponds to evaluating products of the underlying polynomials together with their derivatives up to order \(s-1\).  For an HRS code \(C=HRS_t(\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r\},s)\) the space of such products is spanned by the evaluations of all polynomials of degree at most \(2t-2s\) together with their derivatives up to order \(s-1\).  Thus the Schur square \(C^{\ast2}\) has dimension equal to the number of independent monomials that can appear, namely  

\[
\dim(C^{\ast 2}) = \min\{\, rs,\; 2t-2s+1 \,\}.
\]

The hypothesis \(t\le\frac{r+2s-1}{2}\) is equivalent to \(2t-2s+1\le r\); multiplying by \(s\) gives \(2t-2s+1\le rs\).  Hence the minimum is attained by the second term, and the Schur square attains its full possible size.

\[
\boxed{\dim(C^{\ast2}) = 2t - 2s + 1 }.
\]

ANSWER: \(2t - 2s + 1\)
